references.text: Nadab and Abihu offered unauthorized fire before the Lord, which he had not commanded them, and fire came out from the Lord and consumed them. This illustrates the consequence of bringing an unauthorized offering, as warned in Exodus 30:9.
The verse mentions the death of Nadab and Abihu when they offered strange fire before the Lord's presence, confirming the seriousness of the prohibition against foreign incense on the altar.
A reminder that no stranger who is not of Aaron's line shall come near to burn incense before the Lord's presence, so that he does not become like Korah and his company.
Instructions regarding the holy incense to be used on the altar of incense. The verse explains that this special incense was for holy use only, and foreign incense was forbidden.
The description of the altar of incense and its purpose, providing context for the prohibition against foreign incense and other offerings on this specific altar.
Describes the daily burnt offerings to be offered on the altar of burnt offering, not on the altar of incense. This shows the distinction between the two altars and their respective functions.
The book of Hebrews describes the golden altar of incense in the Most Holy Place, referring to the Old Testament sanctuary service as a shadow of Christ's perfect sacrifice.
A theological contrast between ritualistically correct performance and God's rejection of offerings without heartfelt engagement.
Same chapter and theme: The exclusivity of the sanctuary items and the prohibition against desecration or copying.
A prophetic accusation of neglecting the specific sacrificial requirements (burnt offering, grain offering, incense) established in the law.
Complementary rules: Drink offerings are permitted with burnt or grain offerings (Num), but strictly forbidden on the altar of incense (Ex).
